name: North Korea

facts.religion: Officially atheist; the state cult of the Kim family dominates

snapshot: South Korean intelligence said in 2026 that Kim Jong Un's daughter had been designated his successor, as troops and shells sent to Russia brought the regime cash and combat experience.
culture: North Korean culture is built around devotion to the Kim family; portraits of Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il hang in every home. Mass games, with tens of thousands of performers forming images in unison, display collective discipline. Foreign media, especially South Korean dramas, are banned, and possessing them can bring severe punishment.
society: North Korea is one of the world's most closed and repressive states, with political prison camps holding tens of thousands. Chronic food shortages persist. Its nuclear and missile programmes have advanced despite sanctions. Thousands of soldiers fought for Russia in Kursk, and the alliance has brought oil, food and technology.
situation: The Kim family has ruled North Korea since 1948, the world's only communist hereditary dynasty, sustained by a personality cult around the "Paektu bloodline" named after the sacred mountain where Kim Jong Il was supposedly born. Kim Jong Un, now 42, inherited power at 27. In 2026 he took the clearest step yet toward naming a fourth-generation heir, and she is a girl of about 13.

In February, South Korea's intelligence agency told lawmakers that Kim's daughter Ju Ae had been clearly "designated as a successor" (AFP via Citizen Digital). In January state media showed her for the first time at the Kumsusan mausoleum where her great-grandfather and grandfather lie embalmed. The Workers' Party held its Ninth Congress from 19 February, its first in five years, replacing more than half its presidium; Ju Ae was not shown in the hall (Financial News). But at the closing military parade on 25 February she appeared at her father's side in a matching leather coat, walking the red carpet as generals saluted (AFP via Watauga Democrat). Experts caution she is too young even for party membership, and Kim's sister Kim Yo Jong remains powerful. Meanwhile North Korea has never been more secure: it has thousands of troops fighting for Russia, receives Russian technology and money in return, and its nuclear arsenal keeps growing.
power: A totalitarian one-party state. Kim Jong Un is general secretary of the Workers' Party, chairman of the State Affairs Commission and commander of the armed forces; no independent institutions exist. Information is tightly controlled, and political prisoners number in the tens of thousands.
